review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read the definitions it depends on (relativePicardPresheaf_map_mk, mem_relativeEffectiveCartierSubfunctor_obj_iff) and every use of abelMap, abelMap_app_apply and abelMap_app_top across the repo (MultiplicativeAbel, Abel/Degree, Abel/PicZero, Abel/Jacobi). I could not run Lean. The claim that the two simp rules compete on `D * E` and `1` is an inference from how simp rewrites, not an observed failure. I did not check whether Mathlib's `ConcreteCategory.hom` spelling is itself in simp-normal form; the file's own comment says it is. The private `abelClass` is not simp-relevant, because it never appears in the public statements.

findings.problem: The only simp lemma for `(abelMap f).app T (ULift.up D)` is a definitional unfolding. It rewrites the application to `QuotientGroup.mk (LineBundleClass.mk (… D.2 …).isEffectiveCartier.toInvertibleSheaf)⁻¹`, which exposes a proof-dependent projection of `D.2`. The algebraic lemmas are not simp: `abelMap_app_top` (line 108) and `abelMap_app_mul` (MultiplicativeAbel) are plain lemmas. For `abelMap f` applied to `⊤`, `1` or `D * E`, simp would therefore take the unfolding rule and never reach the structural rules. The unfolded form has no canonical simp lemmas left, because the proof argument depends on `D.2`. The repo's own call sites show this: all three uses are manual `rw [abelMap_app_apply …]` (MultiplicativeAbel.lean:46, PicZero.lean:101, and line 112 of this file). Degree.lean:181 uses `simp only [← abelMapMonoidHom_apply, map_pow, …]` to fold back into the monoid-hom form. So the simp-tagged unfolding is not being used as a simp normal form.
findings.proposed_change: Make the algebraic statements the simp interface. Tag `abelMap_app_top` (and `abelMap_app_mul`) `@[simp]`, or state them through `abelMapMonoidHom` and tag `abelMapMonoidHom_apply` so that `(abelMap f).app T (ULift.up D)` normalises to `abelMapMonoidHom f T D`, where `map_one`, `map_mul`, `map_pow` and `map_prod` apply. Remove `@[simp]` from `abelMap_app_apply`, keeping it as an unfolding lemma for `rw`. Alternatively, keep it simp but give it a lower priority, so the structural lemmas win on `⊤` and `D * E`.
findings.benefit: Simp calls on expressions such as `abelMap f` of a product or power of divisors, or of the empty divisor, would reach the homomorphism lemmas. At present they would be unfolded into a proof-dependent line-bundle class that no other simp lemma recognises. Downstream proofs (Abel/Degree, Abel/PicZero, Abel/Jacobi) could replace manual `rw`/`simp only [← abelMapMonoidHom_apply]` steps with plain `simp`.
